SHIP DUKE or YORK 25TH DECEMBER 1817". It is retained so that the retrieving lane's negative can be replayed rather than taken on trust, and for no other use. 49706 LF-terminated lines. Extent as measured by the retrieving lane: Complete optical-text layer of The Book of Common Prayer (Oxford: Clarendon, 1816). Retrieved as a candidate straight English Prayer Book text and rejected on inspection: the layer is largely unreadable, returning no hit for 'prevent and follow', for any Sunday after Trinity heading, or for the running heads. A bounded negative about this digitisation, not about the book. QUOTE FROM THIS ARTIFACT ONLY THROUGH A CHECKED PASSAGE: it is uncorrected recognition, and a raw-line negative over it cannot exclude a differently recognised spelling.
artifacts.rights_basis: The volume was published at Oxford in 1816, and a work first published abroad before 1931 is out of United States copyright; that line is the one guidance/missals.md records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026 and it moves every January, so it is written here as derived for calendar year 2026 and not as a standing rule. Restoration under 17 U.S.C. 104A could not reach it either: ninety-five years from 1816 ran out in 1911, so nothing remained to restore on 1 January 1996. work.description: The prayer book of the Church of England. Its Sunday collects, epistles and gospels inherit the Sarum arrangement, which is why it stands in this collection at all: its Seventeenth Sunday after Trinity carries the collect of the Roman Sixteenth Sunday after Pentecost.
